newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Quiet as clearer direction sought.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Quiet as clearer direction sought.

text.p: Weaker fuel oil swaps and crude values brought high sulphur fuel oil prices lower although the market was quiet on Monday with traders sidelined while seeking new market direction.
"People are looking for a clear picture. They are waiting for physical activities to indicate a market trend but there has been nothing," said one trader.
Amid thin trading interest, a trader lowered its offer of 20,000-tonnes of 180-cst to $99 per tonne from an earlier $101 for early April lifting, traders said.
The 180-cst was offered at $101 per tonne on Friday.
March fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $98.25/$99.25 and April was at $95.50/$96.50, slightly weaker from Friday's $99.50/$100.50 and $95.00/$96.00 respectively.
Chinese buyers remained largely out of the Singapore market, depite some recent fresh enquiries for April cargoes, and some traders were not optimistic that Chinese activities would emerge soon.
Some maintenance turnarounds in the region are expected to support sentiment, traders said.
In Singapore, Mobil's 280,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) refinery will be shut down starting March 15 for a month.
Singapore Refining Company 90,000-bpd crude unit, an 18,000-bpd hydrocracker and a 32,000-bpd visbreaker remained shut. The turnaround would last until late March.
In Japan and South Korea, the turnaround season starts in April and May.
"The turnarounds may digest some stocks but since they have been scheduled, I don't expect a big increase in demand," said one trader.
Traders said supplies are sufficient.
Last week, Kuwait sold a 80,000-tonne cargo to a major at a premium of $1.10 per tonne over Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis for April delivery to Singapore.
LSWR demand remained weak and market talk was thin, traders said.
